questions.question: A turbine engine compressor which contains vanes on both sides of the impeller is a
choices: double entry axial-flow compressor.
single entry axial-flow compressor.
single-entry centrifugal compressor.
double entry centrifugal compressor.
questions.answerText: double entry centrifugal compressor.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A double-entry centrifugal compressor has an impeller that admits air at both sides of its eye. The two inlet paths feed one impeller, allowing more mass flow for a given wheel diameter.

**Engineering principle**
The diffuser is downstream of the impeller and is not what makes a compressor double-entry.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Two sides feed one impeller.

**Memory hook**
Two sides feed one impeller.

**Board tip**
Identify the inlet geometry at the impeller eye.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the diffuser section in a turbine engine?
choices: To increase pressure and reduce velocity.
To convert pressure to velocity.
To reduce pressure and increase velocity.
To maintain velocity while reducing static pressure.
questions.answerText: To increase pressure and reduce velocity.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
The diffuser slows the high-velocity air leaving the impeller and converts some kinetic energy into static pressure before combustion.

**Engineering principle**
The impeller adds energy to the air; the diffuser reduces velocity and recovers pressure.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Impeller accelerates; diffuser slows and recovers pressure.

**Memory hook**
Impeller accelerates; diffuser slows and recovers pressure.

**Board tip**
Track whether the question asks for energy addition or pressure recovery.

questions.question: In an axial-flow compressor, one purpose of the stator vanes at the discharge end of the compressor is to
choices: decrease the velocity, prevent swirling, and decrease pressure.
straighten the airflow and eliminate turbulence.
increase the swirl of the discharge airflow.
increase the velocity and prevent swirling and eddying.
questions.answerText: straighten the airflow and eliminate turbulence.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Discharge stator vanes remove swirl and direct compressor air toward the next stage or diffuser. Their flow guidance helps reduce residual turbulence and sets the correct entry angle.

**Engineering principle**
A rotor adds energy to the air; a stator turns and diffuses it.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Rotor adds work; stator redirects flow.

**Memory hook**
Rotor adds work; stator redirects flow.

**Board tip**
Do not confuse compressor stators with turbine nozzle guide vanes.

questions.question: The air passing through the combustion chamber of a turbine engine is
choices: used only to cool the turbine blades after combustion.
speeded up and heated by the action of the turbines.
used to support combustion and to cool the engine.
entirely combined with fuel and burned.
questions.answerText: used to support combustion and to cool the engine.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Only part of the compressor air is mixed with fuel and burned. The remaining air cools and protects combustor and turbine surfaces and mixes with the hot gas downstream.

**Engineering principle**
Combustion needs less air than the engine ingests; liner holes distribute cooling and dilution air.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
A portion burns fuel; much of the flow cools and dilutes.

**Memory hook**
A portion burns fuel; much of the flow cools and dilutes.

**Board tip**
A combustor does not burn all its airflow.

questions.question: What is meant by a shrouded turbine?
choices: The turbine wheel is enclosed by a protective shroud to contain the blades in case of failure.
The turbine wheel has a shroud or duct which provides cooling air to the turbine blades.
The turbine blades are individually enclosed in hollow cooling sleeves.
The turbine blades are shaped so that their ends form a band or shroud.
questions.answerText: The turbine blades are shaped so that their ends form a band or shroud.
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A shrouded turbine has blade tips joined by a band or shroud. This reduces tip leakage and helps control vibration, although it adds rotating mass.

**Engineering principle**
A shroud is a tip feature; the turbine disk secures the blade roots.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Band at blade tips, disk at blade roots.

**Memory hook**
Band at blade tips, disk at blade roots.

**Board tip**
Identify whether the question refers to the tip or root.

questions.question: Which compressor control system component protects the LPC by venting the air during low power operation?
choices: VSV
VBV
HP compressor bleed valve
LP turbine bleed valve
questions.answerText: VBV
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Variable bleed valves (VBVs) vent or recirculate low-pressure-compressor air during low-speed operation. They reduce LPC loading and help prevent unstable compressor operation.

**Engineering principle**
A VBV manages compressor airflow; a variable stator changes vane angle, while a blow-off valve may discharge air overboard.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
VBV unloads the low-pressure compressor.

**Memory hook**
VBV unloads the low-pressure compressor.

**Board tip**
Know which spool or compressor the valve protects.

questions.question: What happens to the air when it passes through a turbine nozzle guide vane?
choices: It slows down due to the convergent shape
It speeds up due to the convergent shape
It slows down due to the divergent shape
It speeds up due to the divergent shape
questions.answerText: It speeds up due to the convergent shape
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Nozzle guide vanes turn and accelerate hot gas before it reaches the turbine rotor. Their passage area and angle establish the gas velocity and direction at the rotor.

**Engineering principle**
A nozzle guide vane is a stationary turbine stator; the downstream rotor extracts work.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Stationary guide vane directs; rotating blade extracts work.

**Memory hook**
Stationary guide vane directs; rotating blade extracts work.

**Board tip**
Follow the gas path from combustor to turbine rotor.

questions.question: Which cooling method is mainly used to protect the inner liner of the combustor from the intense heat of the combustion gases?
choices: Impingement cooling
Splash cooling
Film cooling
Convection cooling
questions.answerText: Film cooling
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Film cooling lays a thin layer of cooler compressor air over the combustor liner surface. The film separates the metal from the hottest combustion gas.

**Engineering principle**
Film cooling protects the liner surface; internal convection cools passages inside a part.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Film lies along the hot surface.

**Memory hook**
Film lies along the hot surface.

**Board tip**
Ask whether cooling air is on the surface or inside a passage.

questions.question: What happens to pressure of supersonic air when it flows through a convergent nozzle?
choices: It increases
It decreases
It remains constant
It fluctuates
questions.answerText: It increases
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
In a convergent nozzle, supersonic flow decelerates as area decreases and static pressure rises. A convergent-divergent nozzle is needed to continue accelerating a supersonic stream.

**Engineering principle**
For subsonic flow, a convergent nozzle accelerates and lowers static pressure; the Mach regime changes the result.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Convergent accelerates subsonic flow, decelerates supersonic flow.

**Memory hook**
Convergent accelerates subsonic flow, decelerates supersonic flow.

**Board tip**
Always note whether the nozzle flow is subsonic or supersonic.

questions.question: When the engine is running on ground and the aircraft is not moving, what would be the pressure at the inlet section?
choices: Lower than ambient
Higher than ambient
Same as ambient
Inlet pressure is not affected by ambient pressure
questions.answerText: Lower than ambient
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
At a stationary aircraft inlet, inlet losses and diffusion can make local static pressure below ambient at the compressor face, even though the aircraft is not moving.

**Engineering principle**
An inlet should recover pressure efficiently; local pressure depends on inlet geometry and engine airflow.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Stationary does not mean zero engine airflow.

**Memory hook**
Stationary does not mean zero engine airflow.

**Board tip**
Distinguish ambient pressure from pressure at the inlet station.

questions.question: How is anti-ice performed on the air intake nose?
choices: By electrical heaters
By pneumatic boots
By spraying anti-ice fluid
By spraying hot gas
questions.answerText: By spraying hot gas
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Hot compressor bleed air is routed to the inlet nose to prevent or remove ice. The hot air keeps the leading surface above freezing under the approved operating conditions.

**Engineering principle**
Turbine-engine inlet anti-ice commonly uses hot bleed air; propeller anti-ice can use electrical heat or fluid.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Inlet hot-air anti-ice differs from propeller fluid anti-ice.

**Memory hook**
Inlet hot-air anti-ice differs from propeller fluid anti-ice.

**Board tip**
Name the surface being protected before naming the system.

questions.question: How are compressor stages counted?
choices: Counting a rotor followed by a stator is one compressor stage
Counting a stator followed by a rotor is one compressor stage
One blade whether it’s a rotor or a stator is one compressor stage
A pair of rotor and stator is one compressor stage no matter which one is counted first
questions.answerText: Counting a rotor followed by a stator is one compressor stage
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
One axial-compressor stage consists of a rotor row followed by a stator row. The rotor adds energy; the stator redirects the flow and prepares it for the next rotor.

**Engineering principle**
A stage is a rotor-stator pair, not a single blade row.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
One rotor plus one stator equals one stage.

**Memory hook**
One rotor plus one stator equals one stage.

**Board tip**
Count blade rows by function and sequence.

questions.question: What are the two main elements of a centrifugal flow compressor?
choices: Rotor and stator
Impeller and diffuser
Rotor and diffuser
Impeller and rotor
questions.answerText: Impeller and diffuser
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A centrifugal compressor uses an impeller to accelerate air outward and a diffuser to slow it and recover pressure.

**Engineering principle**
The impeller is the rotating element; the diffuser is stationary.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Rotating impeller plus stationary diffuser.

**Memory hook**
Rotating impeller plus stationary diffuser.

**Board tip**
Separate rotating work input from stationary pressure recovery.

questions.question: During engine deceleration or shutdown, which would contract first, the rotors or the casing?
choices: The rotors because of the reduction in centrifugal force
The rotors because of the thermal contraction
The casing because of the reduction in centrifugal force
The casing because of the thermal contraction
questions.answerText: The rotors because of the reduction in centrifugal force
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
As a turbine engine decelerates or shuts down, rotor speed falls and centrifugal growth of the rotor decreases. The rotor contracts before the heavier casing cools and contracts.

**Engineering principle**
Rotor speed changes quickly; the casing has greater thermal inertia and cools more slowly.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Rotor response is fast; casing cooldown lags.

**Memory hook**
Rotor response is fast; casing cooldown lags.

**Board tip**
Separate speed-related contraction from thermal contraction.

questions.question: Which part of an axial flow compressor would static pressure increase?
choices: The rotors
The stators
The Low Pressure Compressor
Both in the rotors and stators
questions.answerText: Both in the rotors and stators
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Static pressure rises through both compressor rotor and stator rows in a multistage axial compressor. The rotor adds total energy; the stator diffuses and redirects the flow so static pressure also recovers there.

**Engineering principle**
A rotor can increase velocity and total pressure while static-pressure behavior depends on its design; stators are diffusers.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Both rows contribute to stage pressure rise by different mechanisms.

**Memory hook**
Both rows contribute to stage pressure rise by different mechanisms.

**Board tip**
Distinguish static pressure from total pressure.

questions.question: What happens to the airflow as it enters the combustion chamber?
choices: A big part of it is mixed with fuel and burned while the smaller part is used to cool the metal components
A small part of it is mixed with fuel and burned while the bigger part is used to cool the metal components
All of it is mixed with fuel and burned
All of it is used to cool the metal components
questions.answerText: A small part of it is mixed with fuel and burned while the bigger part is used to cool the metal components
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
Only a small part of combustor air supports burning; most bypasses the flame zone to cool the liner and mix with the hot gas. This protects metal and establishes turbine-inlet temperature.

**Engineering principle**
Primary-zone air stabilizes combustion; dilution and cooling air control temperatures downstream.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Burning air is a fraction of total combustor flow.

**Memory hook**
Burning air is a fraction of total combustor flow.

**Board tip**
Look for primary, cooling, or dilution air in the wording.

questions.question: What is the primary function of turbine blades in a gas turbine engine?
choices: To compress incoming air before it enters the combustion chamber.
To extract energy from hot gases and drive the turbine rotor.
To meter fuel into the combustion chamber.
To slow the exhaust before it leaves the engine.
questions.answerText: To extract energy from hot gases and drive the turbine rotor.
questions.explanation: Turbine blades extract energy from the hot gas stream and transfer it to the turbine rotor, which drives the compressor and engine accessories.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions is usually not acceptable to any extent in turbine blades?
choices: Cracks
Pits
Dents
Holes
questions.answerText: Cracks
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A crack in a turbine blade is unacceptable because centrifugal and gas-bending stresses act on a hot, highly loaded component. A small crack can grow rapidly and lead to blade release or secondary damage.

**Engineering principle**
Crack acceptance differs from superficial coating marks or approved blendable damage; use the engine manual?s limits.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
A crack is a flaw with growth potential.

**Memory hook**
A crack is a flaw with growth potential.

**Board tip**
Do not apply generic airframe repair limits to hot-section blades.

questions.question: An advantage of the centrifugal-flow compressor is its _____.
choices: pressure rise per stage
ram efficiency
steady temperature
peak efficiency
questions.answerText: pressure rise per stage
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A centrifugal compressor can produce a comparatively large pressure rise in one stage. Its robust construction and good pressure rise come with a larger frontal area than an axial compressor.

**Engineering principle**
Axial compressors achieve high overall pressure through many stages and smaller frontal area.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Centrifugal: high rise per stage; axial: many compact stages.

**Memory hook**
Centrifugal: high rise per stage; axial: many compact stages.

**Board tip**
Compare pressure rise per stage with frontal area.

questions.question: A weak fuel to air mixture along with normal airflow through a turbine engine may result in _____.
choices: a lean die-out
a rich flameout
very low fuel supply
high EGT
questions.answerText: a lean die-out
questions.explanation:
**Why this is correct**
A weak fuel-air mixture can cause a turbine engine to flame out or lean die out because the combustor cannot sustain stable burning. Normal airflow alone cannot keep the flame lit without adequate fuel scheduling.

**Engineering principle**
A lean die-out is combustion instability or flame extinction; it is not compressor surge.

**Differentiate similar concepts**
Too little fuel can extinguish the combustor flame.

**Memory hook**
Too little fuel can extinguish the combustor flame.

**Board tip**
Distinguish flameout from airflow instability.

questions.question: What is compressor surge in a gas-turbine engine?
choices: A severe breakdown of stable compressor airflow that can cause pressure oscillations and possible flow reversal.
A normal increase in exhaust temperature during cruise.
A decrease in propeller pitch during feathering.
A rise in oil pressure caused by cold oil.
questions.answerText: A severe breakdown of stable compressor airflow that can cause pressure oscillations and possible flow reversal.
questions.explanation:
Surge is an unstable compressor operating condition involving large flow and pressure fluctuations; it can damage engine components.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is the usual function of variable stator vanes in an axial compressor?
choices: Change vane angle to maintain suitable airflow and compressor stability over the operating range.
Meter fuel directly into the combustion chamber.
Cool the turbine blades with oil.
Reverse exhaust flow for braking.
questions.answerText: Change vane angle to maintain suitable airflow and compressor stability over the operating range.
questions.explanation:
Variable stators adjust the airflow angle into following rotor stages as engine speed changes.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: Where is a gas-turbine diffuser normally located in relation to a centrifugal compressor impeller?
choices: Downstream of the impeller.
Ahead of the engine inlet.
Inside the turbine nozzle.
Between the exhaust cone and tailpipe.
questions.answerText: Downstream of the impeller.
questions.explanation:
The diffuser receives high-velocity air leaving the impeller and slows it to recover static pressure.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What happens to airflow velocity through a subsonic compressor diffuser?
choices: It decreases while static pressure increases.
It increases while static pressure increases without limit.
It remains constant while temperature falls.
It reverses direction through every diffuser.
questions.answerText: It decreases while static pressure increases.
questions.explanation:
A diffuser converts some flow kinetic energy into static pressure by reducing velocity.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is a spool in a multi-spool gas-turbine engine?
choices: A compressor and turbine section connected by a shaft and rotating as one assembly.
A fuel-control lever connected to the cockpit.
A group of fuel nozzles in one combustor can.
The stationary outer engine case.
questions.answerText: A compressor and turbine section connected by a shaft and rotating as one assembly.
questions.explanation:
Each spool is a rotating compressor-turbine assembly; different spools may operate at different speeds.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: Why can a multi-spool engine improve compressor operation across a wider range?
choices: Its compressor sections can rotate at different speeds suited to their airflow conditions.
It eliminates all compressor blades.
It forces every compressor stage to turn at the same speed.
It makes the engine independent of inlet air.
questions.answerText: Its compressor sections can rotate at different speeds suited to their airflow conditions.
questions.explanation:
Independent spool speeds let low- and high-pressure compressor sections operate closer to their efficient ranges.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an accessory gearbox on a turbine engine?
choices: Use engine drive to operate accessories such as pumps and generators.
Increase the bypass ratio of the fan.
Mix fuel and air inside the combustor.
Change the area of the exhaust nozzle only.
questions.answerText: Use engine drive to operate accessories such as pumps and generators.
questions.explanation:
The accessory gearbox transfers mechanical power from the engine to required accessories.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: In a turbine engine, what is the role of the turbine nozzle guide vanes?
choices: Direct and accelerate hot gas onto the turbine rotor at the intended angle.
Atomize fuel before it enters the fuel manifold.
Reduce compressor inlet pressure to ambient.
Prevent the compressor from rotating.
questions.answerText: Direct and accelerate hot gas onto the turbine rotor at the intended angle.
questions.explanation:
Nozzle guide vanes direct the combustor gas flow and set its angle and velocity before the turbine rotor.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a turbine-engine exhaust nozzle?
choices: Convert gas pressure and thermal energy into an accelerated exhaust stream.
Increase fuel pressure before combustion.
Drive the accessory gearbox directly.
Cool the combustion chamber by circulating oil.
questions.answerText: Convert gas pressure and thermal energy into an accelerated exhaust stream.
questions.explanation:
The nozzle expands and accelerates the exhaust flow to produce thrust.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.

questions.question: What does the fan on a high-bypass turbofan primarily do?
choices: Accelerate a large mass of bypass air to produce a substantial share of thrust.
Compress fuel for the high-pressure pump.
Drive the ignition exciter without a shaft.
Remove all airflow from the core.
questions.answerText: Accelerate a large mass of bypass air to produce a substantial share of thrust.
questions.explanation:
A high-bypass fan produces much of the engine thrust by accelerating bypass air.

Reference: Powerplant study notes, Laws of Thermodynamics and Thermodynamic Processes; FAA-H-8083-32B, Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook?Powerplant.
